note: REAL verifier output, confirmed by running reference/standalone/verify_envelope.py, impl/go/cmd/scpe-verify, and impl/rust's scpe-verify binary (all three agree on status; detail wording differs per CONTRIBUTING.md's stated contract -- Python: 'manifest unparsable: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM...'; Go: 'manifest unparsable: invalid character... looking for beginning of value'; Rust: 'manifest unparsable: expected value at line 1 column 1'). manifest.json begins with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF), signed as part of the manifest bytes (not mutated after signing). All three JSON parsers reject BOM-prefixed input as invalid JSON, which the Python reference verifier's `except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError)` branch (verify_envelope.py step 2) maps to the status signature-invalid. MINOR NOTE (label precision, not a bypass): this is actually a PARSE failure, not a cryptographic signature failure -- the manifest was never even hashed/checked against the signature, since parsing happens first. The signature itself may well have been valid. The `detail` string does say 'manifest unparsable' so the real cause is not hidden, but the top-level `status` enum has no distinct value for 'well-signed but unparsable payload' -- it is folded into signature-invalid. Not a security issue (both routes correctly refuse to reach verified), just a UX/diagnostic imprecision worth the spec owner knowing about.
